questions.a: 'has been waiting' — 'since' + ongoing duration → present perfect continuous. A wrong answer 'is waiting' shows the student anchors to present instead of the since-marker — the most common class-8 slip.

questions.q: 'By the time the guests arrived, we ___ (finish) cooking.'
questions.a: 'had finished' — 'by the time' orders two past events; earlier takes past perfect. A wrong answer 'finished' flattens the ordering the marker encodes.

questions.q: Which is correct: 'I am knowing him for years' or 'I have known him for years'?
questions.a: The second — 'know' is stative and 'for years' demands the perfect family. A wrong answer accepting the first shows both the stative-ing error and marker-blindness at once.

questions.q: ______ ('has been waiting') is the tenth cell — duration up to a reference point.
Fill in the blank: By class 8 the tense system has nine working cells: three times × three aspects (simple, ______, perfect).
Fill in the blank: The duration test separates the perfects: 'I have waited an hour' (state, completed feel) vs 'I have been waiting an hour' (______ waiting — duration emphasized).
What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student places verbs into all ten cells correctly, reads marker words to pre-select the tense, and distinguishes 'for/since' perfect-continuous use from simple perfect.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: The duration test separates the perfects: 'I have waited an hour' (state, completed feel) vs 'I have been waiting an hour' (still waiting — duration ______).
Fill in the blank: Since + starting point (since ______), for + duration (for two years).
